entities.name: Claude Hardy
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Claude Hardy (1604–1678) was a French mathematician, philologist, and lawyer who was one of the founding members of Marin Mersenne's scientific circle in Paris — the informal academy that was a precursor to the French Academy of Sciences. Hardy was a close associate of Pierre de Fermat and helped transmit Fermat's mathematical discoveries to the Parisian mathematical community. He was also a significant scholar of ancient languages, including Arabic — contributing to the polymath tradition of the 17th-century French intellectual world. His legal career as a councillor in the Paris Parlement coexisted with his mathematical and philological work — the dual life of the gentleman-scholar that characterized the era's intellectual culture.

He translated ancient mathematical texts and corresponded with the leading mathematicians of his day.

He was a member of the Mersenne circle that shaped early modern French mathematics.

He was the lawyer-mathematician of Paris's first scientific community.
